messages:
maria: Heads-up — brought up reranker v2 in staging, seeing global NDCG@10 +0.03 vs v1 on the shortquery holdout. Anyone see obvious suspects? attaching quick logs.
jon: Nice. Are we comparing per-query mean or a global weighted aggregate? small changes in aggregation can make lifts look bigger :thinking:
sam: We're currently using the default harness weighted-average NDCG@10. I also computed per-query median and mean — median is basically flat. suspect candidate pool or dedupe changes.
maria: We did flip dedupe on for v2 (drop exact duplicate docs to reduce apparent duplicates). Could that nudge NDCG?
jon: Yep. If dedupe reduces pool size for queries that had many duplicates, you can get higher NDCG because fewer low-quality duplicates are counted. Also check candidate ordering tie-breakers.
sam: Quick config snapshot from staging:
```
eval_config:
  ctx_pad: 128
  batch_size: 64
  dedupe: true
  scoring_quantized: true
```
sam: Note: v1 used ctx_pad 64 and scoring was fp32; v2 scoring head is int8-quantized for latency tests.
maria: Quantization of the scorer head + dedupe + padding change — lots of moving parts. Also, aggregation by docs vs by queries might amplify the delta. Can we run both macros?
jon: Please run mean_per_query (macro) and global_weighted (micro). Also compute MRR and candidate_count distribution.
sam: Ran a quick pass: global_weighted NDCG +0.030, mean_per_query NDCG +0.004, mean MRR -0.002. So aggregation is the main driver. Posting a small sample CSV now:
qid,ndcg_v1,ndcg_v2,delta,candidate_count_v1,candidate_count_v2
3421,0.412,0.438,+0.026,12,9
8890,0.301,0.360,+0.059,7,4
1122,0.780,0.782,+0.002,10,10

maria: That aligns — qids with reduced candidate_count saw the biggest jumps. Can you also export seed/ordering parity and any sampling logs? I'm worried about nondeterminism from batching.
eval-bot: Auto-eval finished: summary for run v2_vs_v1: global_ndcg:+0.030 | mean_per_query:+0.004 | mean_mrr:-0.002 | artifacts: https://redwood/evals/12345
jon: Action items: (1) sam upload per-query diffs + candidate counts; (2) infra confirm quant seed parity & deterministic scoring; (3) maria run ablation: dedupe on/off and ctx_pad 64/128 on a 5k slice. I'll coordinate a canary if ablation doesn't show regression.
sam: On it — will post artifacts and a small notebook with the per-q diffs and candidate histograms in the next ~45m. @maria @jon
